note: agent-lifted from VA's manuals (pilot steps 2 and 3)

concepts.label: Transmit laser failure
concepts.gloss: A hard fault in the local card's or far-end transmitter's optical laser that extinguishes the transmitted channel and leaves its receiver without light.
concepts.example: A VA-TPD-400 laser fails, causing EQPT_TX_FAIL locally and OCH_LOS at the far-end receiver.

concepts.label: Card failure
concepts.gloss: A hard hardware failure of a local card or far-end transmitting card that can remove received traffic and light, silence monitoring, and mask consequent traffic alarms.
concepts.example: A VA-MXP-400 card loses hardware function, raises EQPT_CARD_FAIL, and its peer reports OCH_LOS while traffic alarms are masked.

concepts.label: Receiver degradation
concepts.gloss: A soft impairment of the receiver electronics or optics on the current card that raises receive errors while the optical path and other channels can remain normal.
concepts.example: One VA-OTN-LC-400 receiver develops excess pre-FEC errors and raises OTU_SD even though neighboring wavelengths remain healthy.

concepts.label: Laser ageing
concepts.gloss: An incipient deterioration of the current card's transmit laser, evidenced by increasing laser-bias current and predictive of eventual laser failure.
concepts.example: A transponder's bias current rises above 120% of its beginning-of-life value, causing LASER_BIAS_HIGH before any loss of light.

concepts.label: Margin erosion
concepts.gloss: An incipient loss of a channel's performance margin that appears as a slow receiver-observed decline, commonly from cumulative component ageing along the path.
concepts.example: Over several months a channel's measured margin falls from 4 dB to 1.5 dB without an abrupt outage.

concepts.label: Fibre break
concepts.gloss: A physical cut or discontinuity in an upstream fibre, particularly the incoming span, that interrupts optical propagation.
concepts.example: An excavator cuts the incoming fibre span, causing AMP_INPUT_LOS and OSC_LOS at the next amplifier hut.

concepts.label: EDFA dead
concepts.gloss: A hard failure of the current or preceding EDFA that produces no amplifier output and can remove every carried wavelength downstream.
concepts.example: An in-line VA-OA-ILA loses its pump completely, raises AMP_FAIL, and all channels disappear at the next node.

concepts.label: jumper pulled
concepts.gloss: A disconnected optical jumper upstream, especially at an OMS input, that removes the optical feed into the section.
concepts.example: A technician unplugs the OMS input jumper, causing AMP_INPUT_LOS on the receiving pre-amplifier.

concepts.label: ROADM ingress port blocked
concepts.gloss: An upstream ROADM ingress port state or fault that prevents light entering the onward optical path.
concepts.example: A WSS ingress port is inadvertently closed, and the downstream transponder raises OCH_LOS for the blocked wavelength.

concepts.label: high span loss
concepts.gloss: Excessive attenuation on an upstream optical span, potentially reducing received power enough to cause amplifier input loss, signal degradation, or OTU frame loss.
concepts.example: A damaged splice adds 12 dB loss to the incoming span, producing AMP_INPUT_LOS and OTU_LOF downstream.

concepts.label: EDFA noise figure degradation
concepts.gloss: A soft upstream EDFA impairment that lowers OSNR while its output power can remain at the expected level.
concepts.example: An ageing amplifier still outputs its target power but adds enough noise for a coherent receiver to raise OTU_SD.

concepts.label: DGD increase
concepts.gloss: An upstream increase in differential group delay that impairs a coherent channel's polarization components and can cause errors or loss of OTU framing.
concepts.example: A polarization event raises DGD beyond receiver tolerance, resulting in OTU_LOF despite light remaining present.

concepts.label: WSS passband offset
concepts.gloss: A soft upstream WSS frequency-response misalignment that shifts or narrows one channel's passband, reducing signal quality despite normal output power.
concepts.example: A WSS filter drifts 5 GHz off-center; channel power remains normal, but pre-FEC BER rises and OTU_SD is raised.

concepts.label: fast SOP event
concepts.gloss: An upstream state-of-polarization change faster than the receiver can track, causing transient coherent-receiver errors.
concepts.example: A rapid fibre polarization transient exceeds DSP tracking speed and creates a burst of errored seconds.

concepts.label: contaminated connector
concepts.gloss: Dirt or residue on an upstream optical connector that introduces loss or reflection and degrades channel quality.
concepts.example: Cleaning a dirty patch-panel connector removes the pre-FEC errors that had caused OTU_SD.

concepts.label: Any failure
concepts.gloss: A generic failure anywhere downstream on the relevant active, working, or protection ODU path when the specific defect class is not distinguished.
concepts.example: A defect on the active ODU path makes the client port raise CLIENT_SF and switch to protection.

concepts.label: Gain loss
concepts.gloss: A soft gain deficiency in the current amplifier card that lowers output power and downstream OSNR.
concepts.example: A pre-amplifier delivers 3 dB less gain than provisioned, raising AMP_GAIN_OOR and reducing all-channel OSNR.

concepts.label: Pump ageing
concepts.gloss: Incipient wear of the current EDFA pump laser that requires progressively higher drive current to maintain gain and ultimately triggers an end-of-life alarm.
concepts.example: PUMP-I climbs to 123% of beginning-of-life current and the EDFA raises AMP_PUMP_EOL.

concepts.label: Gain tilt
concepts.gloss: A soft wavelength-dependent amplifier gain imbalance that leaves channels at one edge of the optical band at low input power downstream.
concepts.example: An EDFA tilt makes the longest-wavelength channels 4 dB weaker than center-band channels.

concepts.label: Fabric failure
concepts.gloss: A hard fault in the current or another OTN cross-connect switch fabric that interrupts traversing client services and forwards ODU-AIS downstream.
concepts.example: VA-OTNSW fabric failure raises OTN_FABRIC_FAIL, sends ODU-AIS on its cross-connected ODUs, and drops their clients.

concepts.label: Misconnection
concepts.gloss: A hard ODU switching or provisioning error at a cross-connect that routes one ODU to the wrong destination without necessarily producing an optical-layer symptom.
concepts.example: An ODU intended for client A is cross-connected to client B, causing ODU_TIM while wavelength power remains normal.

concepts.label: Port failure
concepts.gloss: A hard failure of a client interface port at either service endpoint that takes the associated client service down.
concepts.example: A VA-CP-100GE port fails, raises EQPT_PORT_FAIL, and interrupts its 100GbE client service.

concepts.label: WSS attenuation drift
concepts.gloss: A soft WSS defect in which one channel's attenuation slowly rises above its configured value and reduces downstream channel power.
concepts.example: A channel configured for 3 dB attenuation drifts to 6 dB and arrives downstream at low power.

concepts.label: WSS ingress port failure
concepts.gloss: A hard failure of one WSS ingress port that locally blocks every channel entering through that port while channels on other ROADM degrees remain unaffected.
concepts.example: One ingress module fails, dropping all wavelengths from the west degree but leaving north-degree traffic operational.

concepts.label: No light at the receiver
synonyms: A card with no input light
concepts.gloss: An optical loss-of-signal condition in which one channel has no detectable input light at the receiver, potentially leading to no output and loss of OTU framing.
concepts.example: The far-end receiver measures no input power and raises OCH_LOS after the transmitter fibre is disconnected.

concepts.label: Loss of OTU frame
synonyms: loss of frame if much larger
concepts.gloss: A condition in which an OTU receiver cannot recover valid OTU framing, including cases where optical light is still present, causing downstream ODU-AIS and returned OTU-BDI.
concepts.example: Severely degraded OSNR destroys frame lock; the receiver sends ODU-AIS downstream and OTU-BDI to the transmitter.

concepts.label: Card hardware fault
concepts.gloss: A detected equipment-level hardware defect on a card that can cause OTU frame loss and suppress lower-level traffic alarms.
concepts.example: A line-card ASIC failure raises EQPT_CARD_FAIL, after which related traffic alarms are masked.

concepts.label: traffic alarms masked by the equipment alarm
concepts.gloss: A suppression state in which traffic-layer alarms are hidden because an equipment alarm already identifies the underlying card failure.
concepts.example: After EQPT_CARD_FAIL is asserted, the management system suppresses the card's consequent OTU_LOF indications.

concepts.label: Degraded light: low power, low OSNR, high DGD, passband penalty, receiver penalty, slow margin decline
concepts.gloss: A composite optical degradation state comprising low power, poor OSNR, margin decline, or related DGD, passband, and receiver penalties that can progress from errors to OTU frame loss.
concepts.example: A channel with low power and OSNR first raises OTU_SD and later OTU_LOF as its margin is exhausted.

concepts.label: Errors
synonyms: Pre-FEC errors once the degradation is larger than the channel margin
Errors above the degrade threshold (margin under about 1 dB)
concepts.gloss: Receiver-local bit errors, particularly elevated pre-FEC errors after channel margin falls below the degradation threshold, without necessarily losing frame.
concepts.example: A receiver reports pre-FEC BER above its degrade threshold and raises OTU_SD while remaining frame-locked.

concepts.label: Fast SOP change beyond tracking speed
concepts.gloss: A polarization-state transition whose rate exceeds the coherent receiver's tracking capability and therefore produces errored seconds.
concepts.example: A  rapid SOP rotation during fibre work outruns the DSP and records three errored seconds.

concepts.label: Errored seconds
concepts.gloss: Performance intervals, counted in seconds, during which one or more qualifying transmission errors occur.
concepts.example: A short polarization transient causes the client performance counter to record five errored seconds in a 15-minute bin.

concepts.label: ODU-AIS is sent downstream
synonyms: The switch forwards ODU-AIS on each ODU it cross-connects.
concepts.gloss: The consequent-action state in which ODU alarm indication signal is transmitted on affected ODUs toward downstream clients, taking those services down.
concepts.example: Following OTU_LOF, the receiver inserts ODU-AIS into every ODU carried by that OTU.

concepts.label: OTU-BDI is returned
synonyms: Far end reports a defect on this card's transmitted signal
concepts.gloss: The state in which OTU backward defect indication is sent upstream to tell the far-end transmitter that its transmitted OTU is defective at the receiver.
concepts.example: A receiver that loses OTU framing returns OTU-BDI, which appears as OTU_BDI on the transmitting card.

concepts.label: Laser off or failed
concepts.gloss: A one-channel transmitter state in which the optical laser emits no usable light and includes detection of a transmit-laser fault.
concepts.example: A disabled laser produces zero channel output and the card reports a transmit laser fault.

concepts.label: received traffic lost
concepts.gloss: A local condition in which the traffic arriving at a card is no longer recoverable or available.
concepts.example: After the receive-side card fails, its local received-traffic counters stop and the service drops.

concepts.label: monitoring silent
concepts.gloss: A condition in which the affected equipment supplies no monitoring telemetry or status.
concepts.example: A failed card stops updating power and performance counters in the management system.

concepts.label: normal
concepts.gloss: An unaffected state in which the optical path or channels other than the specifically impaired receiver continue to operate normally.
concepts.example: One receiver raises errors, but all other channels on the same optical path remain within limits.

concepts.label: LBC rising
concepts.gloss: An upward trend in transmit laser bias current that indicates the laser needs more drive to maintain output.
concepts.example: The laser-bias metric rises from 100% to 115% of its beginning-of-life value over six months.

concepts.label: precedes transmit laser failure
concepts.gloss: A predictive state indicating that the observed deterioration occurs before and warns of a future transmit-laser failure.
concepts.example: A sustained high bias-current trend is logged weeks before the laser finally stops emitting.

concepts.label: Slow decline of the channel's margin, usually from ageing of components along the path
concepts.gloss: A gradual reduction in one channel's receiver-observed operating margin, usually caused by cumulative ageing along its path.
concepts.example: Daily telemetry shows channel margin declining by 0.1 dB per month at the receiver.

concepts.label: Transmit laser fault detected
concepts.gloss: An equipment diagnostic state asserting that the transmitter's laser has an internal or output failure.
concepts.example: The card detects absent laser output despite an enable command and raises EQPT_TX_FAIL.

concepts.label: LBC above 120 % of beginning of life (internal supervision)
concepts.gloss: An internally supervised threshold condition in which transmit laser bias current exceeds 120% of its beginning-of-life reference.
concepts.example: A bias-current reading of 122% satisfies the condition and raises LASER_BIAS_HIGH.

concepts.label: The EDFA cards run in automatic gain control (AGC).
concepts.gloss: The operating state in which EDFA cards regulate their gain automatically rather than holding a fixed output power.
concepts.example: An in-line EDFA adjusts pump current after input power changes so that its configured gain is maintained.

concepts.label: The gain target is provisioned at turn-up equal to the attenuation of the fibre span ahead of the card.
concepts.gloss: An EDFA provisioning rule that sets the turn-up gain target equal to the loss of the following fibre span.
concepts.example: For an 18 dB outgoing span, the amplifier is commissioned with an 18 dB gain target.

concepts.label: Under AGC, a drop of input level
synonyms: An upstream power loss within that range
concepts.gloss: An AGC operating event in which amplifier input power falls, leading according to magnitude and control range to low output, degraded OSNR, node levelling, or propagated low channel power.
concepts.example: A 5 dB input drop causes AGC to compensate power partly, but the downstream OSNR penalty remains.

concepts.label: low output
synonyms: an equal drop of output level
concepts.gloss: An amplifier output-power condition below the expected level across all carried channels.
concepts.example: Composite output drops 4 dB below target and every downstream wavelength is correspondingly weak.

concepts.label: OSNR down
synonyms: the optical signal-to-noise ratio (OSNR) of all channels degrades with it
the OSNR penalty it caused stays
concepts.gloss: A downstream optical signal-to-noise-ratio degradation affecting one or all channels even when nominal signal power may be restored.
concepts.example: AGC restores channel power after an upstream loss, but all downstream channels retain a 2 dB OSNR penalty.

concepts.label: no output light
synonyms: No light at OUT-PWR with input light present
concepts.gloss: A condition in which an optical device emits no output light across all channels, possibly despite having input light.
concepts.example: An EDFA has normal input power but zero OUT-PWR and raises AMP_FAIL.

concepts.label: Other conditions at the input
concepts.gloss: A collective state for input impairments other than the specifically treated level change, which the amplifier does not correct.
concepts.example: Input spectral ripple enters an EDFA as an 'other condition' and is reproduced at its output.

concepts.label: are passed through to the output
concepts.gloss: A propagation state in which conditions present at a device input remain present at its output.
concepts.example: An input channel's passband distortion remains visible after amplification.

concepts.label: Every hut terminates the optical supervisory channel (OSC) and launches its own OSC onto the next span
concepts.gloss: A network design condition in which each amplifier hut receives the incoming OSC and originates a new OSC for the next span.
concepts.example: Hut B terminates Hut A's OSC and launches a separate OSC toward Hut C.

concepts.label: an OSC failure is confined to the span on which it occurs
concepts.gloss: A fault-containment condition in which loss of an OSC affects only its individual fibre span rather than propagating through later huts.
concepts.example: Loss of the A-to-B OSC raises OSC_LOS at B, while B's newly generated OSC to C remains operational.

concepts.label: all channels lost
concepts.gloss: A complete multiwavelength outage in which every optical channel in the affected aggregate is absent.
concepts.example: A dead line amplifier removes all 80 wavelengths from the outgoing span.

concepts.label: output power normal
concepts.gloss: A state in which aggregate or single-channel output power remains within its expected range despite another impairment such as degraded OSNR or passband shape.
concepts.example: A noisy EDFA maintains target output power while the receiver observes lower OSNR.

concepts.label: PUMP-I climbs to maintain gain
concepts.gloss: An EDFA ageing indication in which the local pump-drive current increases to preserve the configured gain.
concepts.example: The amplifier raises pump current from 100% to 118% of baseline while holding 20 dB gain.

concepts.label: ends in the end-of-life alarm
concepts.gloss: The terminal stage of a local card's ageing trend at which an end-of-life alarm is asserted.
concepts.example: Continued pump-current growth eventually crosses 120% and raises AMP_PUMP_EOL.

concepts.label: low in power
synonyms: is passed on as low power
concepts.gloss: A below-normal optical input-power state affecting one channel or channels at one band edge and observable downstream.
concepts.example: Only the high-frequency edge channels arrive 3 dB below their expected receiver power.

concepts.label: OSC not received
concepts.gloss: A state in which an amplifier or pre-amplifier cannot detect the optical supervisory channel on its incoming span.
concepts.example: The line OSC disappears after a span cut, causing the downstream hut to raise OSC_LOS.

concepts.label: Gain more than 2 dB from target
concepts.gloss: An amplifier regulation condition in which actual gain differs from its provisioned target by more than 2 dB.
concepts.example: Measured gain is 16.5 dB against a 19 dB target, so AMP_GAIN_OOR is raised.

concepts.label: PUMP-I above 120 % of beginning of life
concepts.gloss: An EDFA pump-age threshold state in which pump-laser drive current exceeds 120% of its beginning-of-life value.
concepts.example: A pump current of 124% triggers AMP_PUMP_EOL.

concepts.label: a misdirected ODU
concepts.gloss: An ODU connectivity condition in which a payload is delivered along the wrong cross-connect path, causing the intended client service to fail.
concepts.example: ODU2 from port 1 is routed to port 7 instead of port 5, leaving the intended client down.

concepts.label: the client service down
concepts.gloss: An unavailable client-service state caused at a client optic, port, or traversed ODU set, including interruption through an OTN switch.
concepts.example: A switch-fabric failure interrupts every ODU through the switch and the attached Ethernet clients go down.

concepts.label: ODU-AIS or a misdirected ODU
concepts.gloss: A received ODU defect state consisting of either ODU-AIS or delivery of an ODU on the wrong connection, potentially causing only a brief protected-service hit.
concepts.example: The working path presents ODU-AIS, so SNCP selects the healthy protection path after a short traffic hit.

concepts.label: SNCP is configured
concepts.gloss: A service configuration state in which ODU traffic uses subnetwork connection protection with working and protection paths.
concepts.example: A client is provisioned with disjoint working and protection ODUs terminating at the same selector.

concepts.label: the selector has a defect-free path to choose
concepts.gloss: A protection state in which the receive-side selector has at least one ODU path without a detected defect.
concepts.example: The working ODU fails, but the selector finds the protection ODU defect-free and switches to it.

concepts.label: the service takes a hit only
concepts.gloss: A protected-service outcome in which traffic suffers only a transient disturbance rather than a sustained outage.
concepts.example: SNCP switching causes a 30 ms interruption, after which the client service continues on protection.

concepts.label: cross-connected to the wrong destination
concepts.gloss: A one-ODU switching state in which the ODU is connected to an unintended egress or client endpoint.
concepts.example: An ODU expected on port A emerges on port B and causes an ODU_TIM mismatch.

concepts.label: no optical symptom
concepts.gloss: A state in which an ODU-layer defect exists but optical power and other optical-layer indicators remain normal.
concepts.example: A misconnected ODU raises ODU_TIM although per-channel power and OSNR show no fault.

concepts.label: Switching is per channel
concepts.gloss: A ROADM switching property in which each wavelength is independently routed rather than an ingress line being switched as one aggregate.
concepts.example: Three wavelengths arriving on the west degree are independently sent to three different egress degrees.

concepts.label: A line-wide impairment on an ingress degree therefore continues as a per-channel impairment on each channel routed onward.
concepts.gloss: The propagation result whereby an impairment common to an ingress line becomes an individual impairment on every wavelength routed from that line to later degrees.
concepts.example: Low power on the west ingress appears separately on each west-originating channel routed north and east.

concepts.label: is levelled out at the node
concepts.gloss: A power-control outcome in which a node restores a channel or aggregate level to its target, although quality penalties may remain.
concepts.example: The ROADM equalizer restores a weak channel to nominal output power but cannot restore its lost OSNR.

concepts.label: passes through
concepts.gloss: A propagation state in which an impairment traverses a network element without being removed or materially changed.
concepts.example: A channel's low OSNR passes through the next EDFA even though its power is amplified.

concepts.label: Attenuation creeps above its setting
concepts.gloss: A one-channel WSS state in which actual attenuation gradually exceeds the configured attenuation value.
concepts.example: A WSS setting remains 4 dB while measured attenuation slowly increases to 6 dB.

concepts.label: Passband shifted
concepts.gloss: A one-channel filter condition in which the WSS transmission passband center is displaced from the channel frequency.
concepts.example: The passband center shifts 4 GHz away from the carrier and clips one side of its spectrum.

concepts.label: Passband narrowed
concepts.gloss: A one-channel filter condition in which the usable WSS bandwidth is smaller than intended and clips the signal spectrum.
concepts.example: A nominal 50 GHz passband contracts to 38 GHz, degrading the coherent signal.

concepts.label: signal quality down
concepts.gloss: A degradation of one channel's recoverable optical signal quality, such as reduced margin or increased BER, without implying total signal loss.
concepts.example: Power remains normal after a WSS offset, but pre-FEC BER rises and receiver margin falls.

concepts.label: blocked
concepts.gloss: A local state in which one ingress path prevents all of its channels from passing onward.
concepts.example: A failed WSS ingress port blocks every wavelength arriving from the west degree.

concepts.label: unaffected
concepts.gloss: A state indicating that resources or traffic on ROADM degrees other than the failed one continue without impairment.
concepts.example: The west ingress fails, but channels arriving on the north and east degrees remain operational.

concepts.label: Received optical power
concepts.gloss: The measured optical power entering a receiver, available through standard or licensed power monitoring.
concepts.example: A VA-TPD-400 reports received optical power of -14.2 dBm for its line channel.

concepts.label: errored seconds
concepts.gloss: A performance counter recording seconds containing qualifying client or transport errors, available as standard monitoring.
concepts.example: The card records 12 client errored seconds in the current 15-minute bin.

concepts.label: OSNR
concepts.gloss: The measured optical signal-to-noise ratio of a channel, exposed through advanced monitoring or an OCM licence.
concepts.example: A ROADM OCM reports an OSNR of 18.5 dB for channel 37.

concepts.label: pre-FEC BER
concepts.gloss: The bit-error ratio measured before forward-error correction, used to quantify receiver input quality under advanced monitoring.
concepts.example: A coherent line card reports pre-FEC BER of 2×10^-3 while corrected traffic remains error-free.

concepts.label: DGD
concepts.gloss: The measured differential group delay between polarization modes of a coherent optical signal, available with advanced monitoring.
concepts.example: A VA-OTN-LC-400 reports DGD increasing from 8 ps to 35 ps during a polarization event.

concepts.label: SOP rate of change
concepts.gloss: The measured rate at which the received signal's state of polarization changes, used to identify events beyond receiver tracking speed.
concepts.example: Advanced monitoring records an SOP rotation rate spike coincident with errored seconds.

concepts.label: Transmit laser bias current, % of beginning of life
concepts.gloss: The transmitter laser's present bias current expressed as a percentage of its beginning-of-life reference, used as an ageing indicator.
concepts.example: A transponder reports laser bias at 121%, crossing the LASER_BIAS_HIGH threshold.

concepts.label: Composite input power
concepts.gloss: The total optical power of all wavelengths entering an EDFA, available under the power-monitoring licence.
concepts.example: A VA-OA-ILA reports composite input power of -8 dBm across 40 channels.

concepts.label: Composite output power
concepts.gloss: The total optical power of all wavelengths leaving an EDFA, available under the power-monitoring licence.
concepts.example: The amplifier reports +18 dBm composite output while operating at its target gain.

concepts.label: Pump laser drive current, % of beginning of life
concepts.gloss: An EDFA pump laser's drive current expressed as a percentage of its beginning-of-life reference, used to track pump ageing.
concepts.example: Advanced monitoring shows pump drive current at 123%, prompting AMP_PUMP_EOL.

concepts.label: OSC receiver status
concepts.gloss: The standard status indication of whether an EDFA's optical supervisory-channel receiver is receiving and decoding the incoming OSC.
concepts.example: After a span cut, the pre-amplifier's OSC receiver status changes from received to not received.

concepts.label: client UAS
concepts.gloss: The standard client unavailable-seconds performance counter measuring time during which the client service is considered unavailable.
concepts.example: A failed client port accumulates 60 client UAS during a one-minute outage.

concepts.label: Per-channel power
concepts.gloss: The optical power measured separately for each wavelength by an optical channel monitor under an OCM licence.
concepts.example: The ROADM reports channel 21 at -3 dBm and channel 22 at -6 dBm.

concepts.label: VA-TPD-400
concepts.gloss: The VA 400G transponder resource that terminates an optical channel and measures receive power, errors, OSNR, pre-FEC BER, DGD, SOP dynamics, and laser ageing.
concepts.example: A deployed VA-TPD-400 measures -12 dBm receive power and 20 dB OSNR on a 400G wavelength.

concepts.label: VA-MXP-200
concepts.gloss: The VA 200G muxponder resource that aggregates client traffic onto a 200G line signal and provides coherent optical and performance measurements.
concepts.example: A VA-MXP-200 carries multiple clients and reports their line channel's pre-FEC BER and DGD.

concepts.label: VA-MXP-400
concepts.gloss: The VA 400G muxponder resource that aggregates client traffic onto a 400G line signal and supplies coherent-channel and laser-health telemetry.
concepts.example: A VA-MXP-400 reports 19 dB OSNR and 110% laser-bias current for its 400G carrier.

concepts.label: VA-OTN-LC-200
concepts.gloss: The VA 200G OTN line card that terminates a 200G OTU and measures its optical quality, errors, polarization behavior, and transmitter bias.
concepts.example: A VA-OTN-LC-200 raises OTU_SD when its measured pre-FEC BER exceeds the degrade threshold.

concepts.label: VA-OTN-LC-400
concepts.gloss: The VA 400G OTN line card that terminates a 400G OTU and exposes coherent optical, performance, and transmitter-health measurements.
concepts.example: A VA-OTN-LC-400 detects high DGD and subsequently raises OTU_LOF.

concepts.label: EDFA card
concepts.gloss: A VA erbium-doped fibre-amplifier card usable as a booster, in-line amplifier, or pre-amplifier and able to monitor composite powers, pump ageing, and OSC status.
concepts.example: A VA-OA-ILA measures -10 dBm input, +17 dBm output, and pump current at 112% of baseline.

concepts.label: transmit-side EDFA (booster), fitted at the head end of each optical multiplex section (OMS)
concepts.gloss: An EDFA deployed at the transmitting head end of an OMS to boost the multiplexed optical signal into the outgoing span.
concepts.example: A VA-OA-BST raises the ROADM aggregate to +20 dBm before launch into a long fibre span.

concepts.label: optical line amplifier (OLA), fitted at in-line amplifier huts
concepts.gloss: An EDFA deployed at an intermediate amplifier hut to restore optical level between OMS endpoints.
concepts.example: A VA-OA-ILA in a mid-span hut supplies 18 dB gain and can raise AMP_INPUT_LOS on loss of incoming light.

concepts.label: receive-side EDFA (pre-amp), fitted at the tail end of each OMS
concepts.gloss: An EDFA deployed at the receiving tail end of an OMS to amplify weak incoming channels before demultiplexing or reception.
concepts.example: A VA-OA-PRE amplifies the incoming line and reports OSC_LOS when the span supervisory channel disappears.

concepts.label: All
concepts.gloss: The collective resource class covering every EDFA deployment role: transmit booster, in-line OLA, and receive pre-amplifier.
concepts.example: AMP_FAIL may be raised by any of VA-OA-BST, VA-OA-ILA, or VA-OA-PRE.

concepts.label: OTN cross-connect switch
concepts.gloss: An OTN switching-fabric resource that cross-connects ODUs between interfaces and can propagate ODU-AIS when its fabric fails.
concepts.example: A VA-OTNSW routes an ODU2 between line cards and raises OTN_FABRIC_FAIL if the switch fabric fails.

concepts.label: client interface port
concepts.gloss: A physical client-facing service port on VA equipment for Ethernet or another client signal, represented by 10GE, 100GE, and 400GE port models.
concepts.example: A VA-CP-100GE terminates a customer's 100GbE service and raises CLIENT_SF when that signal fails.

concepts.label: colourless, directionless, contentionless ROADM
concepts.gloss: A CDC ROADM that independently routes any wavelength between degrees without fixed colour, direction, or contention constraints and can monitor per-channel power and OSNR.
concepts.example: A VA-ROADM-CDC routes the same wavelength from any add port to the east degree while its OCM measures channel power.

concepts.label: one WSS module per degree
concepts.gloss: The ROADM implementation unit consisting of a separate wavelength-selective-switch module for each line direction or degree.
concepts.example: A four-degree ROADM contains four WSS modules, so one west-degree ingress failure need not affect the other three.

concepts.label: OCH_LOS
concepts.gloss: A critical optical-channel loss-of-signal alarm raised by supported transponder, muxponder, or OTN line cards when one receiver has no light, with likely upstream laser, card, fibre, EDFA, jumper, or ROADM blockage causes.
concepts.example: A fibre cut removes one wavelength at a VA-TPD-400 receiver, which reports OCH_LOS.

concepts.label: OTU_LOF
concepts.gloss: A critical OTU loss-of-frame alarm raised by supported coherent cards when OTU framing is unrecoverable, often from severe upstream optical degradation or receiver impairment.
concepts.example: Low OSNR causes a VA-OTN-LC-400 to lose frame lock and raise OTU_LOF while light remains present.

concepts.label: OTU_SD
concepts.gloss: A minor OTU signal-degrade alarm raised by supported coherent cards when receiver errors exceed the degradation threshold but framing is retained.
concepts.example: A contaminated connector increases pre-FEC BER and a VA-MXP-200 raises OTU_SD.

concepts.label: OTU_BDI
concepts.gloss: A non-alarming OTU backward-defect indication reported by supported line equipment when the far end signals a defect in the locally transmitted OTU.
concepts.example: After the remote receiver loses frame, the local VA-TPD-400 records OTU_BDI without assigning an alarm severity.

concepts.label: EQPT_TX_FAIL
concepts.gloss: A critical equipment alarm raised by supported transmitting cards when an internal transmit-laser fault is detected.
concepts.example: A VA-MXP-400 detects zero laser output despite enablement and raises EQPT_TX_FAIL.

concepts.label: EQPT_CARD_FAIL
concepts.gloss: A critical equipment alarm raised by supported transport cards for a detected card-level hardware fault.
concepts.example: An ASIC failure on a VA-OTN-LC-200 raises EQPT_CARD_FAIL and masks consequent traffic alarms.

concepts.label: LASER_BIAS_HIGH
concepts.gloss: A minor ageing alarm raised by supported cards when internally supervised transmit-laser bias current exceeds 120% of its beginning-of-life value.
concepts.example: A VA-TPD-400 reports 122% laser bias and raises LASER_BIAS_HIGH.

concepts.label: AMP_INPUT_LOS
concepts.gloss: A critical amplifier input loss-of-signal alarm, also named OMS_LOS_P, raised by an OLA or pre-amplifier when incoming optical light is absent.
concepts.example: A pulled OMS jumper causes a VA-OA-PRE to raise AMP_INPUT_LOS.

concepts.label: OSC_LOS
concepts.gloss: A major incoming-span alarm raised by an OLA or pre-amplifier when its OSC is not received, commonly because of a fibre break or excessive span loss.
concepts.example: A cut between huts A and B makes B's VA-OA-ILA report OSC_LOS against the A-to-B span.

concepts.label: AMP_FAIL
concepts.gloss: A critical alarm available on any EDFA role when the amplifier has no output light, indicating a dead EDFA.
concepts.example: A booster pump fails completely, output falls to zero, and AMP_FAIL is raised.

concepts.label: AMP_GAIN_OOR
concepts.gloss: A minor OLA or pre-amplifier alarm raised when measured gain differs from target by more than 2 dB, potentially from amplifier death, gain loss, or pump ageing.
concepts.example: A pre-amplifier provides 16 dB against a 19 dB target and raises AMP_GAIN_OOR.

concepts.label: AMP_PUMP_EOL
concepts.gloss: A minor alarm on any EDFA role indicating pump drive current above 120% of its beginning-of-life value due to pump ageing.
concepts.example: A VA-OA-ILA reaches 125% pump current and raises AMP_PUMP_EOL before losing gain.

concepts.label: CLIENT_SF
concepts.gloss: A critical signal-fail alarm raised by a client interface port when its client service fails because of a path, port, cross-connect, or fabric defect.
concepts.example: A VA-CP-100GE raises CLIENT_SF after its active ODU path fails.

concepts.label: ODU_AIS
concepts.gloss: A non-alarming client-port indication that ODU alarm indication signal is being received for the associated ODU.
concepts.example: Following an upstream OTU_LOF, the receiving client port records ODU_AIS while the root alarm remains upstream.

concepts.label: ODU_BDI
concepts.gloss: A non-alarming client-port indication that ODU backward defect indication has been received or returned for the associated ODU connection.
concepts.example: A far-end ODU defect causes the local client port to report ODU_BDI as a consequential indication.

concepts.label: ODU_TIM
concepts.gloss: A major client-port alarm indicating an ODU trail-trace identifier mismatch, typically revealing a misconnection.
concepts.example: An ODU is cross-connected to the wrong client port, whose expected trace differs and triggers ODU_TIM.

concepts.label: PROT_ACTIVE
concepts.gloss: A minor client-port alarm indicating that protection is carrying the service because a failure affected the preferred or active ODU path.
concepts.example: An SNCP selector switches from the failed working path to protection and raises PROT_ACTIVE.

concepts.label: PROT_UNAVAIL
concepts.gloss: A minor client-port alarm indicating that an ODU protection path is unavailable because of a failure, reducing path redundancy.
concepts.example: The working path still carries traffic, but failure of the standby path raises PROT_UNAVAIL.

concepts.label: EQPT_PORT_FAIL
concepts.gloss: A critical client-interface equipment alarm indicating a hard failure of the local client port.
concepts.example: A failed VA-CP-400GE optical interface raises EQPT_PORT_FAIL and drops the client service.

concepts.label: OTN_FABRIC_FAIL
concepts.gloss: A critical alarm raised by the OTN cross-connect switch when its internal switching fabric fails.
concepts.example: VA-OTNSW loses a fabric plane, raises OTN_FABRIC_FAIL, and sends ODU-AIS on affected cross-connects.

concepts.label: one channel
concepts.gloss: The impact scope limited to a single optical wavelength or transmitted channel rather than the whole multiplex.
concepts.example: A WSS passband offset degrades channel 37 while channels 36 and 38 remain normal.

concepts.label: received traffic
concepts.gloss: The scope consisting of traffic arriving at the affected receiver or card.
concepts.example: A local card failure removes the traffic being received on its line interface.

concepts.label: monitoring
concepts.gloss: The scope consisting of telemetry, supervision, and performance reporting functions.
concepts.example: A dead card stops publishing all of its power and BER measurements.

concepts.label: traffic alarms
concepts.gloss: The scope consisting of alarms derived from carried traffic rather than equipment hardware.
concepts.example: OTU and ODU alarms are masked after a card hardware alarm identifies the root fault.

concepts.label: this receiver only
concepts.gloss: An impact boundary restricted to the particular receiving endpoint observing the defect.
concepts.example: Receiver degradation raises errors on one coherent receiver but not at other receivers on the path.

concepts.label: other channels
concepts.gloss: The optical wavelengths sharing a system other than the specifically affected channel.
concepts.example: One channel loses frame while the other 79 channels remain normal.

concepts.label: the optical path
concepts.gloss: The end-to-end optical route traversed by a wavelength between its transmitter and receiver.
concepts.example: The optical path remains healthy even though one receiver's electronics are degraded.

concepts.label: LBC
concepts.gloss: The transmit laser-bias-current quantity used to assess laser drive and ageing.
concepts.example: The observed impact is a rise in LBC from 100% to 118% of baseline.

concepts.label: transmit laser failure
concepts.gloss: The future transmit-laser failure event to which an incipient warning or precursor applies.
concepts.example: A rising-bias condition is classified as preceding the eventual transmit laser failure.

concepts.label: the channel's margin
concepts.gloss: The selected channel's remaining performance headroom before errors or loss of framing occur.
concepts.example: OSNR degradation reduces the channel margin from 3 dB to 0.8 dB.

concepts.label: all channels
synonyms: all channels arriving on that degree
concepts.gloss: The complete set of wavelengths carried in the affected optical aggregate or arriving on the affected degree.
concepts.example: A dead EDFA removes every channel on the outgoing fibre.

concepts.label: this card
concepts.gloss: The particular equipment card on which the condition is detected or contained.
concepts.example: Pump-current ageing telemetry applies to the local VA-OA-ILA card only.

concepts.label: channels at one band edge
concepts.gloss: The subset of wavelengths near one extreme of the amplified optical band.
concepts.example: Gain tilt lowers only the longest-wavelength channels at the edge of the C-band.

concepts.label: All ODUs
concepts.gloss: Every optical data unit carried by the relevant OTU, switch, or failed fabric.
concepts.example: Loss of an OTU causes ODU-AIS to be sent on each ODU multiplexed within it.

concepts.label: One ODU
concepts.gloss: A single optical data unit trail or connection, excluding other ODUs sharing the infrastructure.
concepts.example: A bad cross-connect misdirects one ODU while the switch's other ODUs remain correct.

concepts.label: Client optic
concepts.gloss: The client-facing optical transceiver associated with a service endpoint.
concepts.example: Failure of the 100GE client optic takes its attached service down.

concepts.label: port
concepts.gloss: One physical or logical interface, including a client port or a single WSS input port.
concepts.example: A WSS fault blocks one west-degree input port rather than the entire ROADM.

concepts.label: client service
concepts.gloss: The customer-facing traffic service delivered through the transport network.
concepts.example: A fabric failure makes the customer's 100GbE service unavailable.

concepts.label: other degrees
concepts.gloss: ROADM line directions other than the ingress or egress degree affected by the fault.
concepts.example: A west-degree WSS failure leaves north, south, and east degrees unaffected.

concepts.label: the far-end receiver
concepts.gloss: The remote receiving endpoint opposite the local transmitter, where transmitted-light loss is observed.
concepts.example: A local laser failure appears as OCH_LOS at the far-end receiver.

concepts.label: locally
concepts.gloss: At the current network element or node rather than elsewhere along the path.
concepts.example: A failed WSS ingress port shows all of its channels blocked locally at the ROADM.

concepts.label: the receiver
concepts.gloss: The optical receiving function where channel quality, margin, and errors are measured.
concepts.example: A slow margin decline becomes visible in telemetry at the coherent receiver.

concepts.label: Far-end transmitter
concepts.gloss: The remote transmitting endpoint that sends the signal into the current receiver.
concepts.example: No light at the local receiver is traced to a failed laser in the far-end transmitter.

concepts.label: Upstream on the path
synonyms: Anywhere upstream on the channel's path
concepts.gloss: Any point earlier in the signal's propagation route relative to the observing receiver or node.
concepts.example: A contaminated connector two nodes before the receiver is upstream on the channel path.

concepts.label: This card
concepts.gloss: The specific local circuit card being diagnosed or reporting the condition.
concepts.example: A rising pump current is localized to this VA-OA-ILA rather than the preceding amplifier.

concepts.label: downstream
synonyms: on the path to the far end
concepts.gloss: Any point later in the direction of signal or traffic flow, toward the far-end destination after the current node.
concepts.example: An EDFA noise penalty remains measurable at all receivers downstream of that amplifier.

concepts.label: one band edge
concepts.gloss: One frequency extreme of the supported optical band where tilt-related channel weakness is concentrated.
concepts.example: Only channels near the long-wavelength C-band edge show low power.

concepts.label: the incoming span
concepts.gloss: The fibre section terminating at the observing node or amplifier from the immediately preceding site.
concepts.example: OSC_LOS at Hut B is reported against the incoming span from Hut A.

concepts.label: previous EDFA
concepts.gloss: The immediately preceding optical amplifier in the upstream signal path.
concepts.example: No input light at the current OLA is traced to the previous EDFA's failed pump.

concepts.label: OMS input
concepts.gloss: The physical input point where the optical multiplex section enters a node or amplifier.
concepts.example: A jumper pulled from the OMS input causes the pre-amplifier to lose all incoming light.

concepts.label: through the switch
concepts.gloss: Along ODU connections traversing the internal OTN cross-connect fabric.
concepts.example: A fabric fault interrupts every affected client service passing through the switch.

concepts.label: on the active ODU path
concepts.gloss: At any point on the ODU route currently selected to carry protected service traffic.
concepts.example: A failure on the active ODU path makes the selector move traffic to the standby route.

concepts.label: at either end
concepts.gloss: At either of the two terminating endpoints of a bidirectional client or ODU service.
concepts.example: A client-port failure at either endpoint can take the end-to-end service down.

concepts.label: at a switch on the ODU path
concepts.gloss: At an intermediate OTN cross-connect traversed by the ODU connection.
concepts.example: A misconnection at the second switch routes the ODU to the wrong destination.

concepts.label: on the working ODU path
concepts.gloss: At any point on the ODU route designated as the normal working member of a protected pair.
concepts.example: A fibre fault on the working ODU path causes SNCP to select protection.

concepts.label: on the protection ODU path
concepts.gloss: At any point on the standby ODU route intended to protect the working path.
concepts.example: A defect on the protection ODU path raises PROT_UNAVAIL while working traffic continues.

concepts.label: This port
concepts.gloss: The particular local interface port being monitored or diagnosed.
concepts.example: EQPT_PORT_FAIL identifies this VA-CP-100GE port as the failed component.

concepts.label: This switch
concepts.gloss: The particular local OTN cross-connect whose fabric or switching behavior is under diagnosis.
concepts.example: OTN_FABRIC_FAIL localizes the fault to this VA-OTNSW.

concepts.label: Standard
concepts.gloss: The base monitoring entitlement supplied without a specialized licence, including ordinary status and 15-minute performance bins.
concepts.example: Client errored seconds are available in standard 15-minute bins without an advanced licence.

concepts.label: Power monitoring licence
concepts.gloss: A licensed feature entitlement that exposes optical power measurements such as received or composite input and output power.
concepts.example: After enabling the power-monitoring licence, an EDFA reports composite input and output power.

concepts.label: Advanced monitoring licence
concepts.gloss: A licensed feature entitlement that exposes advanced coherent and ageing metrics such as OSNR, pre-FEC BER, DGD, SOP rate, and laser currents.
concepts.example: Enabling advanced monitoring makes DGD and transmit-laser bias telemetry visible on a VA-TPD-400.

concepts.label: OCM licence
concepts.gloss: A licensed optical-channel-monitor capability that exposes per-wavelength power and OSNR measurements.
concepts.example: With an OCM licence, a VA-ROADM-CDC reports power and OSNR for each channel.

concepts.label: Hard
concepts.gloss: A fault nature denoting an abrupt, definite equipment or connectivity failure that commonly causes loss of signal or service.
concepts.example: A dead EDFA is hard because its output disappears and all channels are immediately lost.

concepts.label: Soft
concepts.gloss: A fault nature denoting partial degradation in quality or level while the affected equipment or signal may remain operational.
concepts.example: An EDFA noise-figure degradation is soft because output power remains normal while OSNR worsens.

concepts.label: Incipient
concepts.gloss: A fault nature denoting an early deterioration trend that precedes a likely future hard failure or end-of-life threshold.
concepts.example: Rising laser-bias current is incipient because traffic still passes while the laser ages.

concepts.label: Critical
concepts.gloss: The highest operational alarm class here, assigned to defects that directly threaten or interrupt signal, equipment, or service operation.
concepts.example: OCH_LOS is reported as critical because the optical channel has no received light.

concepts.label: Minor
concepts.gloss: A lower operational alarm class for degradation, ageing, or protection states that require attention but may not currently interrupt service.
concepts.example: LASER_BIAS_HIGH is minor because it predicts ageing while the channel can still carry traffic.

concepts.label: Not alarmed
concepts.gloss: A classification for consequential or informational defect indications that are reported but do not themselves create an active alarm.
concepts.example: OTU_BDI is recorded as not alarmed because the actionable root defect is at the remote receiver.

concepts.label: Major
concepts.gloss: A serious alarm class below critical, used here for significant supervisory or connectivity defects requiring prompt action.
concepts.example: OSC_LOS is major because span supervision is lost even though payload channels may still be present.

concepts.label: On loss of OTU frame, G.798 consequent actions apply: ODU-AIS is sent downstream on every ODU in the OTU, and OTU-BDI is returned to the far-end transmitter.
concepts.gloss: The G.798 fault-propagation behavior whereby OTU frame loss makes the receiver send ODU-AIS on every contained ODU and return OTU-BDI toward the source.
concepts.example: When an OTU carrying four ODUs loses frame, all four downstream ODUs receive AIS and the transmitting endpoint receives OTU-BDI.

concepts.label: Every hut terminates the optical supervisory channel (OSC) and launches its own OSC onto the next span.
concepts.gloss: The OSC regeneration behavior whereby each amplifier hut terminates the incoming supervisory channel and originates a separate OSC on the next span, containing failures per span.
concepts.example: An OSC failure from Hut A to B is detected at B but does not prevent B from transmitting its own OSC to Hut C.

concepts.label: Client services may be protected with SNCP: a working and a protection ODU path, with the selector at the receiving client port.
concepts.gloss: The service-protection behavior in which an SNCP-protected client has separate working and protection ODU paths selected at the receiving client port.
concepts.example: When the working ODU develops AIS, the receive-port selector chooses the defect-free protection ODU after only a brief hit.

concepts.label: Switching is per channel at each egress degree. A line-wide impairment on an ingress degree therefore continues as a per-channel impairment on each channel routed onward.
concepts.gloss: The ROADM forwarding behavior whereby wavelengths are switched independently at each egress degree, so a line-wide ingress impairment follows each affected channel onto its chosen onward route.
concepts.example: A power loss on the west ingress follows west-originating channel 10 to the north degree and channel 20 to the east degree as separate channel impairments.
